newsitem.title: USA: Report raps both U.S., Swiss over Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Report raps both U.S., Swiss over Nazi gold.

text.p: A U.S. study released on Wednesday criticized both the Swiss and American governments of the time for their handling of Nazi gold after the Second World War.

The document criticised the United States for not pushing Switzerland hard enough once the war ended to account for and return the gold it had acquired in financial deals with the Nazis during the war.

"There was a demonstrable lack of senior-level support for a tough U.S. negotiating position with the neutrals (countries)," including Switzerland, said the study, which was compiled by Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat and the State Department's chief historian, William Slaney.

"Serious shortcomings in U.S. and Allied policy" led to the loss of most leverage before Switzerland had met its obligations to return Nazi gold from countries and Holocaust victims from which it had been taken, the report said.

As a neutral country, Switzerland had "one of the most complex roles in World War II," but its "business as usual" attitude in resisting the return of looted Nazi gold afterwards was "inexplicable," the report said.
